extracted.intended_audience: FCC employees, agency ethics officials, potential donors, local governments/associations, licensees/applicants, and counsel preparing petitions or seeking declaratory rulings or waivers under 47 CFR Part 1
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural requirements for (1) acceptance, evaluation, and disclosure of gifts to the Commission; (2) preemption/waiver and challenge procedures for restrictions that impair reception or fixed wireless signals; and (3) filing, content, and foreign-ownership compliance methodology for petitions under section 310(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions for gift-acceptance subpart
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of this subpart: (a) the term agency means the Federal Communications Commission. (b) the term gift means any unconditional gift, donation or bequest of real, personal and other property (including voluntary and uncompensated services as authorized under 5 U.S.C. 3109). (c) the terms agency ethics official, designated agency ethics official, employee, market value, person, and prohibited source, have the same meaning as found in 5 CFR 2635.102, 2635.203.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the definitional baseline for applying the gift-acceptance rules and cross-references government-wide meanings in 5 CFR part 2635.

rubrics_metrics.name: General prohibitions on gifts
rubrics_metrics.description: An employee shall not: (1) Directly or indirectly, solicit or coerce the offering of a gift, donation or bequest to the Commission from a regulated entity or other prohibited source; or (2) Accept gifts of cash pursuant to this subpart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absolute prohibition on solicitation/coercion from regulated entities and on accepting cash gifts; frames conduct that would disqualify acceptance under the subpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral of gift offers to designated agency ethics official
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person who seeks to offer any gift to the Commission under the provisions of this subpart shall make such offer to the Commission's designated agency ethics official. Any Commission employee contacted by a potential donor or representative for the purpose of discussing making a gift shall immediately refer such person(s) to the designated agency ethics official.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designated agency ethics official consults with other agency ethics officials to determine conflict/appearance of conflict, may advise potential donors about useful items and procedures, and the Commission may give public notice before accepting gifts. All donor-offers must be funneled to the ethics official—employees must not handle acceptance negotiations themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory factors for evaluating conflicts of interest (gift acceptance)
rubrics_metrics.description: No gift shall be accepted under this subpart unless a determination is made that its acceptance would not create a conflict of interest or the appearance of a conflict of interest. Designated agency ethics officials shall consider the following factors: (a) whether benefits accrue to an individual employee and, if so, whether the employee is responsible for matters affecting the potential donor currently before the agency and the significance of the employee's role; (b) the nature and sensitivity of any matters pending at the Commission affecting the intended donor; (c) the timing of the intended gift; (d) the market value of the intended gift; (e) the frequency of other gifts made by the same donor; and (f) the reason underlying the intended gift given in a written statement from the proposed donor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptance requires affirmative determination that no real or apparent conflict exists; each of the listed factors is to be weighed (including written donor explanation) before acceptance is approved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public disclosure and recordkeeping for accepted gifts
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission's Security Operations Office shall maintain a written record of gifts accepted from prohibited sources pursuant to section 4(g)(3) authority, including: (1) identity of the prohibited source; (2) description of the gift; (3) market value; (4) documentation concerning the prohibited source's reason for the gift as required in § 1.3003(f); (5) a signed statement from the prohibited source that the gift is unconditional and not contingent on any promise or expectation that the Commission's receipt will benefit the donor in any regulatory matter; and (6) the date the gift is accepted. The Commission shall also file a semi-annual report to Congress listing the gift, donor and value of all gifts accepted under this subpart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed documentation and verification requirements for accepted gifts; emphasizes unconditional nature of gifts and periodic congressional reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of restrictions that impair reception (prohibited restrictions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any restriction (including state or local laws/regulations, zoning, building regs, private covenants, lease provisions, homeowners' association rules, or similar restrictions) on property within the exclusive use or control of the antenna user that impairs installation, maintenance, or use of: (i) antennas 1 meter or less used to receive direct broadcast satellite service or to receive/transmit fixed wireless signals via satellite (and antennas located in Alaska); (ii) antennas 1 meter or less used to receive video programming via multipoint distribution services or to receive/transmit fixed wireless signals other than via satellite; (iii) antennas used to receive television broadcast signals; or (iv) a mast supporting such antennas, is prohibited to the extent it so impairs (subject to paragraph (b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the classes of small/consumer antennas and masts protected from restrictive regulation on property under the user's control; prohibition applies to any restriction that 'impairs' as defined elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of fixed wireless signals (scope exclusions)
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of this section, 'fixed wireless signals' means any commercial non-broadcast communications signals transmitted via wireless technology to and/or from a fixed customer location. Fixed wireless signals do not include AM radio, FM radio, amateur ("HAM") radio, CB radio, and Digital Audio Radio Service (DARS) signals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that the preemption covers commercial fixed wireless services and explicitly lists common radio services that are excluded from this definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: When a restriction 'impairs' installation, maintenance, or use
rubrics_metrics.description: A law, regulation, or restriction impairs installation, maintenance, or use of an antenna if it: (i) unreasonably delays or prevents installation, maintenance, or use; (ii) unreasonably increases the cost of installation, maintenance, or use; or (iii) precludes reception or transmission of an acceptable quality signal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three-prong test used to determine whether a restriction is impermissible under the preemption: delay/prevention, cost-increase, or signal-quality preclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonableness of fees and enforcement protections for antenna users
rubrics_metrics.description: Any fee or cost imposed on a user by a rule, law, regulation or restriction must be reasonable in light of the cost of the equipment or services and the restriction's treatment of comparable devices. No civil, criminal, administrative, or other legal action of any kind shall be taken to enforce any restriction or regulation prohibited by this section except pursuant to paragraph (d) or (e). If a proceeding is initiated, the entity seeking to enforce the restriction must suspend enforcement pending review. No attorney's fees shall be collected or assessed and no fine or other penalties shall accrue against an antenna user while a proceeding is pending. If a ruling is adverse, the user is granted at least a 21-day grace period to comply; no fine or penalty may be collected if the user complies during this period unless the restriction proponent demonstrates the user's claim was frivolous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects users from enforcement while disputes are pending, caps recoverable costs/fees, and provides a grace period and anti-frivolous-claim safeguard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of hub or relay antenna
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of this section, 'hub or relay antenna' means any antenna used to receive or transmit fixed wireless signals for the distribution of fixed wireless services to multiple customer locations as long as the antenna serves a customer on whose premises it is located, but excludes any hub or relay antenna used to provide any telecommunications services or services provided on a commingled basis with telecommunications services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes distribution-oriented fixed wireless antennas (covered) from facilities used to provide telecommunications or commingled telecommunications services (excluded).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted restrictions: safety and historic-preservation exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Any restriction otherwise prohibited is permitted if: (1) it is necessary to accomplish a clearly defined, legitimate safety objective stated in the text/preamble/legislative history or described in a document readily available to antenna users and is applied non-discriminatorily to comparable appurtenances/devices; or (2) it is necessary to preserve a prehistoric or historic district/site/building/structure/object included in or eligible for the National Register of Historic Places and imposes no greater restrictions on antennas than on comparable modern appurtenances/devices; and (3) it is no more burdensome to affected antenna users than necessary to achieve the objectives in (1) or (2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows narrowly tailored restrictions for legitimate safety or historic-preservation aims, but requires clear justification, non-discriminatory application, and minimal burden consistent with objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver application procedures for local governments and associations
rubrics_metrics.description: Local governments or associations may apply to the Commission for a waiver of this section under § 1.3. Waiver requests must comply with the procedures in paragraphs (f) and (h) and will be put on public notice. The Commission may grant a waiver upon a showing of local concerns of a highly specialized or unusual nature. Waivers granted will not apply to restrictions amended or enacted after the waiver is granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waiver applicants must follow specified service/pleading procedures and public-notice rules; waivers are discretionary and limited to demonstrated unusual local concerns; waivers are not perpetual if the underlying restriction is later changed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural timelines for pleadings in waiver and declaratory ruling proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Any responsive pleadings must be served on all parties and filed within 30 days after release of a public notice that such petition has been filed. Any replies must be filed within 15 days thereafter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fixed short timelines for responses and replies in Commission proceedings regarding waivers or declaratory rulings under this section; adherence required for procedural compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of petitions for declaratory rulings and courts of competent jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may petition the Commission for a declaratory ruling under § 1.2, or a court of competent jurisdiction, to determine whether a particular restriction is permissible or prohibited under this section. Petitions to the Commission must comply with the procedures in paragraphs (f) and (h) and will be put on public notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides both administrative (FCC declaratory ruling) and judicial avenues; administrative petitions are subject to the same service and pleading rules as waivers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and constructive notice requirements for petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of petitions for declaratory rulings and waivers must be served on interested parties, including parties against whom the petitioner seeks to enforce the restriction or parties whose restrictions the petitioner seeks to prohibit. A certificate of service stating on whom the petition was served must be filed. In Commission proceedings brought by an association or local government, constructive notice of the proceeding must be given to members/citizens; the petitioner must file with the Commission or court a copy of the constructive notice with a statement explaining where the notice was placed and why such placement was reasonable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes broad service obligations and, when constructive notice is used, the need to document and justify the notice method and placement for public inspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof for restrictions' compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: In any proceeding regarding the scope or interpretation of any provision of this section, the burden of demonstrating that a particular governmental or nongovernmental restriction complies with this section and does not impair installation, maintenance, or use of covered devices shall be on the party that seeks to impose or maintain the restriction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shifts evidentiary burden to the restriction proponent to show compliance and non-impairment in proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit support and filing/inspection requirements for pleadings
rubrics_metrics.description: All allegations of fact contained in petitions and related pleadings before the Commission must be supported by affidavit of a person or persons with actual knowledge thereof. An original and two copies of all petitions and pleadings should be addressed to the Secretary at the FCC's main office (per 47 CFR 0.401(a)). Copies of petitions and related pleadings will be available for public inspection through the Reference Information Center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires factual allegations to be sworn by knowledgeable affiants and prescribes physical filing and public availability procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to file petitions for foreign-ownership approval under section 310(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: A broadcast, common carrier, aeronautical en route or aeronautical fixed radio station licensee or common carrier spectrum lessee shall file a petition for declaratory ruling to obtain Commission approval under section 310(b)(4) and obtain such approval before the aggregate foreign ownership of any controlling U.S.-organized parent company exceeds 25 percent of the U.S. parent's equity interests and/or 25 percent of its voting interests. A common carrier radio station licensee or spectrum lessee shall file a petition for declaratory ruling to obtain approval under the Commission's section 310(b)(3) forbearance approach and obtain such approval before aggregate foreign ownership held through intervening U.S.-organized entities exceeds 20 percent of its equity interests and/or 20 percent of its voting interests. An applicant shall file the petition at the same time it files its application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires prior Commission approval before specified foreign-ownership benchmarks would be exceeded; distinguishes 310(b)(4) (25%) and the 310(b)(3) forbearance (20%) rules and filing timing tied to associated licensing applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing systems and channels for petitions (ICFS/CDBS/ECFS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for petitions involving broadcast stations only, petitions required by paragraph (a) shall be filed electronically through the International Communications Filing System (ICFS) or any successor. Petitions involving broadcast stations only shall be filed electronically through the Media Bureau's Consolidated Database System (CDBS) when submitted as part of an application for a construction permit, assignment, or transfer of control; if no associated application, petitions should be filed with the Office of the Secretary via the Commission's Electronic Comment Filing System (ECFS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the electronic filing system to use based on license/service type and whether the petition accompanies a licensing application; consult ICFS/CDBS/ECFS guidance and subpart Y for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certifications, joint filings, and who may certify
rubrics_metrics.description: Each applicant, licensee, or spectrum lessee filing a petition shall certify to the information contained in the petition in accordance with § 1.16. Multiple applicants and/or licensees shall file jointly the petition where entities are under common control and contemporaneously hold, or are contemporaneously filing applications for, the relevant authorizations. Joint petitioners with different responses should set out such information separately except as otherwise permitted. The controlling parent may certify alternatively; transferees or ultimate controlling parents may file and certify in connection with transfer applications. Multiple applicants and licensees shall not be permitted to file a petition jointly unless under common control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescribes who must certify accuracy of petition contents, when joint filing is required or permitted, and restrictions on joint filings to ensure accurate, auditable submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions for foreign-ownership provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions applicable to §§ 1.5000–1.5004 include: aeronautical radio licenses (en route & fixed only); affiliate (common control >50% voting power); control (actual working control, includes indirect control); entity (partnership, trust, corporation, LLC, governmental authority, etc.); group (two or more acting together to acquire/hold/vote/dispose of equity/voting interests); individual (natural person); licensee (includes spectrum lessee per § 1.9003); privately held company; public company (issued class of equity securities subject to SEC beneficial ownership reporting); subsidiary (>50% voting power); voting stock; would hold (interests proposed to be held upon consummation of transactions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides precise terms used throughout the foreign-ownership rules to determine attribution, control, and applicability of filing obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology for eligible U.S. public companies to identify beneficial owners and equity holders
rubrics_metrics.description: An 'eligible U.S. public company' (organized in the U.S., traded on a U.S. exchange, and with a class of equity securities subject to SEC beneficial ownership reporting) shall use information known or reasonably should be known in the ordinary course of business to identify beneficial owners and equity interest holders, including: (i) information recorded in the company's share register; (ii) shares held by officers, directors, and employees; (iii) information reported in SEC Schedule 13D and 13G (including amendments) and company-specific info from Form 13F; (iv) information in annual/quarterly reports (or proxy statements); (v) identity and citizenship known through litigation, financing transactions, and proxies; and (vi) identity/citizenship known by whatever source. The company shall use known or reasonably should-be-known information to determine citizenship of beneficial owners and equity interest holders and exercise due diligence in identifying/determining citizenship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the ordinary-course sources and due-diligence expectations for public companies to identify who counts as a foreign beneficial owner for the purpose of § 310(b) compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculating aggregate foreign ownership and compliance determination
rubrics_metrics.description: To calculate aggregate levels of foreign ownership, a licensee or spectrum lessee controlled by an eligible U.S. public company shall base calculations on the public company's known or reasonably should be known foreign equity and voting interests. The licensee shall separately aggregate known foreign voting interests and known foreign equity interests. If both the known foreign voting interests and known foreign equity interests do not exceed 25 percent (20 percent for licensees subject to § 310(b)(3)), the company shall be deemed compliant with the applicable statutory limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the aggregation method and thresholds for compliance; includes an illustrative example (e.g., 6 + 4 foreign shares out of 100 total = 10% foreign ownership deemed compliant).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of petitions for declaratory ruling under section 310(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition required by § 1.5000(a)(1) and/or (2) shall contain: (a) for each petitioning applicant or licensee, name; FCC Registration Number (FRN); mailing address; place of organization; telephone; facsimile (if available); email (if available); type of business organization; name and title of officer certifying the petition; (b) if represented, representative's name, firm, mailing address, and telephone/email; (c)(1) for each named licensee, list type(s) of radio service authorized and for broadcast list call sign, facility ID, and community of license or transmit site; (c)(2) if petition filed in connection with an application, specify File No(s) or anticipated filing dates and types of radio services covered; (d) statement whether requesting a declaratory ruling under § 1.5000(a)(1) and/or (2); and (e) disclosable interest holders—direct U.S. or foreign interests in the controlling U.S. parent (applicable to certain petitions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed checklist of factual and administrative information that must be included in a § 310(b) petition to satisfy filing requirements and enable Commission review; subsequent paragraphs (b)-(i) set forth filing mechanics, certification, joint filing rules, and additional disclosure obligations.
